label: Derived table. Elliptic-curve times use rho rates measured in this repository on one GPU type (Curve25519 uses the P-256 rate as a labelled proxy); RSA figures are extrapolated from a cited record; ML-KEM figures are cited and not converted. Not a benchmark or leaderboard row; no number here is pcc-verified.

rows.name: RSA-2048
rows.formula: GPU-years = anchor GPU-years x L(N)/L(anchor), L = L_N[1/3,(64/9)^(1/3)], o(1) = 0
rows.caveat: order of magnitude only: the o(1) term, memory, the linear-algebra share and hardware change are ignored
display_cells: NIST strength 112 bits; GNFS L-ratio to the 862-bit RSA-260 record = 2^36.4
RSA-260 record: 13.5 GPU-years on B200-class GPUs (cited)

inputs.status: Derived table, version 1, drafted 2026-11-22 for review by the Principal Cryptographer (action plan 2026-11-21, row R2). It is not a benchmark, not a leaderboard row and not a validated result. Elliptic-curve rows combine a textbook work formula with a throughput measured and committed in this repository; RSA and ML-KEM rows are cited published estimates. Every input below carries its source; gen_table.rs derives everything else.

rows.name: ECC2K-130 (calibration)
rows.method: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points on classes under negation and Frobenius
rows.automorphisms_basis: negation times the 131 powers of Frobenius (2 x 131)
rows.walk_constant_source: crypto:ecc2k130/WALK-CONSTANT.md section 6: Bailey et al.'s planning budget 2^60.9 is 2^60.809 x 1.069; measured for this walk 1.070-1.082 on completed trails

published_check.source: D. V. Bailey et al., 'Breaking ECC2K-130', IACR ePrint 2009/541 (the planning budget quoted across crypto:ecc2k130/)

repo_cost_check.source: crypto:ecc2k130/aws/README.md cost table and crypto:ecc2k130/FPGA-CEILING.md section 5 (RTX PRO 6000 at 14.11 B/s: 42,400 GPU-hours, $56k spot, $142k on-demand g7e.2xlarge)

rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm solves the ECDLP in polynomial time on a large fault-tolerant quantum computer; none exists today
rows.quantum_source: Roetteler, Naehrig, Svore, Lauter, 'Quantum Resource Estimates for Computing Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms', ASIACRYPT 2017, IACR ePrint 2017/598

rows.name: P-256 (secp256r1)
rows.method: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points and the negation map
rows.walk_constant_source: assumption: idealised random walk; real r-adding walks cost a few percent more (ECC2K-130 measures 1.07-1.08)
rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm; at most 2,330 logical qubits and about 1.29e11 Toffoli gates for a 256-bit prime field by the bounds of the cited paper; no such machine exists today
rows.quantum_source: Roetteler, Naehrig, Svore, Lauter, ASIACRYPT 2017, IACR ePrint 2017/598 (bounds 9n + 2ceil(log2 n) + 10 qubits and 448 n^3 log2 n + 4090 n^3 Toffoli gates, evaluated at n = 256)

rows.name: secp256k1
rows.method: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points, walk on classes under Aut(E) = Z/6 (negation and the GLV endomorphism)
rows.walk_constant_source: assumption: idealised random walk (as for P-256)
rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm (same resource class as P-256); no such machine exists today
rows.quantum_source: Roetteler, Naehrig, Svore, Lauter, ASIACRYPT 2017, IACR ePrint 2017/598

rows.name: Curve25519 / Ed25519
rows.method: parallel Pollard rho with distinguished points and the negation map, in the prime-order subgroup
rows.automorphisms_basis: Aut(E) = {+1, -1}: the j-invariant of y^2 = x^3 + 486662x^2 + x over GF(2^255 - 19) is not 0 or 1728 (checked)
rows.walk_constant_source: assumption: idealised random walk (as for P-256)
rows.rate_note: No rho throughput on the 2^255 - 19 field has been measured in this repository (gpu/ecc compiles Curve25519 vectors for its CPU tests only). The P-256 rate, same field type and size, is used as a labelled proxy; a dedicated 2^255 - 19 reduction could be faster or slower.
rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm; no such machine exists today
rows.quantum_source: Roetteler, Naehrig, Svore, Lauter, ASIACRYPT 2017, IACR ePrint 2017/598

rows.name: RSA-2048
rows.nist_source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 (2020), Table 2: RSA k = 2048 has a 112-bit security strength
rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm; the cited estimate is under a million noisy qubits for less than a week; no such machine exists today
rows.quantum_source: C. Gidney, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits', arXiv:2505.15917 (2025)

rows.name: RSA-3072
rows.nist_source: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 (2020), Table 2: RSA k = 3072 has a 128-bit security strength
rows.quantum_vulnerable: yes: Shor's algorithm; no such machine exists today
rows.quantum_source: C. Gidney, arXiv:2505.15917 (2025), for the RSA-2048 case; RSA-3072 needs somewhat more

rows.name: ML-KEM-512
rows.method: primal lattice attack with BKZ and sieving (core-SVP model and the specification's refined gate count)
rows.lattice_source: Avanzi et al., CRYSTALS-Kyber Algorithm Specifications and Supporting Documentation v3.02 (2021-08-04), Table 4 and section 5.2 ('this number could be affected by a factor of up to 2^16 in either direction'); ML-KEM (FIPS 203, 2024) uses these parameter sets
rows.not_used: the lab's own 'mlwe margins' estimator is excluded until its outside review (action plan R5)
rows.quantum_vulnerable: not known: no quantum algorithm is known that breaks Module-LWE at these parameters beyond the quantum core-SVP figure

rows.name: ML-KEM-768
rows.method: primal lattice attack with BKZ and sieving (core-SVP model and the specification's refined gate count)
rows.lattice_source: Avanzi et al., CRYSTALS-Kyber Algorithm Specifications and Supporting Documentation v3.02 (2021-08-04), Table 4; ML-KEM (FIPS 203, 2024) uses these parameter sets
rows.not_used: the lab's own 'mlwe margins' estimator is excluded until its outside review (action plan R5)
rows.quantum_vulnerable: not known: no quantum algorithm is known that breaks Module-LWE at these parameters beyond the quantum core-SVP figure

gnfs.heuristic_source: the number field sieve's heuristic running time (Buhler, Lenstra, Pomerance, in A. K. Lenstra and H. W. Lenstra (eds.), The Development of the Number Field Sieve, LNM 1554, Springer 1993)

rsa260.source: E. Lu (Cognition), 'Factoring RSA-260': 'about 4,900 GPU-days, or 13.5 GPU-years, which is about $400k at current market prices' (Appendix 1: $414k); modified CADO-NFS with a GPU lattice siever on B200/GB200/GB300. https://cognition.com/blog/factoring-rsa-260

rsa896.source: M. Ivezic, 'RSA-896 Factored With Claude, 16 Days After RSA-260', PostQuantum.com, 2026-09-19, reporting S. A. Weis: about 10 days and roughly 30 GPU-years on up to 2,048 GPUs; GPU model not named; compute not independently confirmed. https://postquantum.com/security-pqc/rsa-896-factored-claude-gpus/

rsa250_cpu.source: Boudot, Gaudry, Guillevic, Heninger, Thomé, Zimmermann, RSA-250 announcement, 2020-02-28: 'roughly 2700 core-years, using Intel Xeon Gold 6130 CPUs as a reference (2.1GHz)'. https://caramba.loria.fr/rsa250.txt
